name: InfluxData, Inc. (formerly Errplane)
origin_detail: Founded in 2012 as Errplane by Paul Dix and Todd Persen, a Y Combinator company. It open-sourced InfluxDB in 2013 and renamed itself InfluxData; based in San Francisco.
openness_notes: InfluxDB is MIT-licensed. In 2016 clustering was taken out of the open-source build and sold in the proprietary InfluxDB Enterprise (open core). The Rust rewrite, InfluxDB 3 Core, is MIT/Apache-2.0 dual licensed, with paid Enterprise and cloud tiers: level 2.

license_history.license: MIT core; clustering moved to proprietary InfluxDB Enterprise

relicensing_events.outcome_note: A feature move rather than a licence change; drew community criticism but no major fork known (unverified)

robustness: Single-vendor, VC-backed; the core stays OSI-licensed, so it is forkable.
openness_effect_assessment: Not assessed: no sourced research was possible in this session.
key_takeaway: Draft only. InfluxData never moved its core off OSI licences; it closed by moving a key feature (clustering) into a paid edition, a quieter form of closing that avoided a licence fight.
